seo.title: Work Agent for Researchers: Evidence Review | Floatboat
seo.description: A Work Agent that organizes research sources, builds evidence matrices, compares findings, drafts reviews, and maintains research briefs.

hero.eyebrow: A Work Agent for evidence preparation
hero.title: A Work Agent for researchers and insight teams
hero.description: Assign Floatboat a defined research task. It can organize selected sources, build evidence matrices, compare findings, and maintain a dated research brief while researchers retain verification and methodological judgment.

burdens.eyebrow: The repetitive work around the profession
burdens.title: researchers and insight teams should not spend their best hours rebuilding context.
burdens.description: Research quality erodes when collection outpaces classification, notes lose their sources, and conflicting findings are flattened into a convenient summary.

items.label: Context
items.title: Source collection outgrows bookmarks
items.description: Search results, papers, reports, datasets, and archived pages quickly exceed what browser tabs and bookmarks can explain.

items.label: Format
items.title: Notes lose their evidence trail
items.description: A useful observation becomes unreliable when its quotation, page, method, publication date, or retrieval context disappears.

items.label: Coordination
items.title: Conflicting findings need structure
items.description: Studies can disagree because of sample, method, scope, or date; a prose summary often hides those reasons.

items.label: Continuity
items.title: Monitoring work never really ends
items.description: New publications keep arriving, but few deserve to reopen the evidence matrix or change the current conclusion.

workflows.eyebrow: Three assignments for a research Work Agent
workflows.title: Build a traceable evidence trail before drawing conclusions.
workflows.description: Each assignment begins with a defined question, source set, and protocol, returns an inspectable result, and stops before interpretation.

items.title: Prepare a literature review
items.job: Turn a defined question and source set into a searchable inventory and thematic synthesis.
items.output: A source inventory, themes, gaps, and review outline.
items.boundary: Researchers verify inclusion criteria, citations, methods, and interpretation.

items.title: Build an evidence matrix
items.job: Compare claims, samples, methods, dates, and limitations across a selected body of work.
items.output: A traceable matrix of findings and limitations.
items.boundary: The researcher resolves ambiguity and decides evidentiary weight.

items.title: Run recurring topic monitoring
items.job: Track selected publications and update a living brief when meaningful evidence appears.
items.output: A dated update with new evidence and unresolved questions.
items.boundary: Humans approve sources and decide whether an update changes the conclusion.

boundaries.note: Floatboat is a general-purpose Work Agent, not an academic database or substitute for a researcher's methodology. It works inside a persistent workspace; data handling depends on the models, tools, connectors, permissions, and research policies selected for that environment.

faq.title: Work Agent questions for researchers and insight teams
faq.description: Researchers need provenance, explicit inclusion rules, and a clear separation between source extraction and interpretation.

items.question: Is Floatboat a reference manager or academic database?
items.answer: No. Keep your authoritative databases and citation manager. Floatboat helps turn a selected source set into searchable notes, comparison tables, research briefs, and repeatable monitoring workflows.

items.question: Can it decide which evidence is credible?
items.answer: It can expose methods, dates, samples, claims, and limitations, but the researcher defines inclusion criteria, resolves ambiguity, weighs evidence, and owns the interpretation.

items.question: Can we define our own review protocol and evidence fields?
items.answer: Yes. Configure the question, databases or source set, date range, inclusion rules, extraction schema, quality checks, and output format for each project.

items.question: How do we prevent fabricated citations or unsupported synthesis?
items.answer: Require every extracted claim to retain its source location, keep unavailable evidence marked as unavailable, and verify citations, quotations, and numerical findings before using the synthesis.

items.question: Can unpublished or restricted research material be used?
items.answer: Only when permissions, agreements, and organizational policy allow it. Separate restricted projects, limit access, and review how each selected model and connector processes the material.

items.question: Will it update a literature review automatically?
items.answer: It can monitor approved sources and draft a dated change brief, but a researcher should decide which new items meet the protocol and whether they alter the review.

items.question: What is a good first research workflow?
items.answer: Choose a small, known corpus and define the extraction fields in advance. Build an evidence matrix, audit it against the originals, and only then expand the source set.

finalCta.title: Carry the source trail into the next synthesis.
finalCta.description: Define the corpus and extraction fields first. Keep each claim traceable when moving the synthesis into a draft.
